section_summary: This section comprises monthly political reports and State Department internal records concerning Japan during the spring and summer of 1934. It contains the Embassy's comprehensive report on conditions in Japan for February 1934, covering naval disarmament policies, cabinet instability, and relations with the United States, Manchukuo, and the Soviet Union. The section also includes an internal Far Eastern Affairs memorandum analyzing reporting practices and Despatch No. 823 transmitting the May 1934 report, which addresses the aftermath of the Amau statement and regional economic initiatives.

subfiles.about: Monthly report on political, foreign, military, and economic conditions in Japan during February 1934.
subfiles.from: Embassy of the United States of America, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: The report provides a detailed survey of Japanese foreign affairs, domestic politics, military matters, and finance during February 1934. It details Foreign Minister Hirota's efforts to ease friction with the United States, debates concerning naval ratios and Pacific defense, and negotiations with the Soviet Union over fisheries and the Chinese Eastern Railway. Domestically, it examines political corruption scandals confronting the Saito Cabinet, the sentencing of civilian conspirators in the May 15 incident, Diet debates on military spending and farm relief, and foreign commercial developments in Manchukuo.
subfiles.title: Report on Conditions in Japan During the Month of February, 1934

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum reviewing the contents and growing length of the Tokyo Embassy's monthly political reports.
subfiles.summary: Memo criticizes the growing length of Tokyo's monthly reports; highlights May 1934 items on Japanese-American diplomacy, Kwantung Army economic affairs, Inner Mongolia and Netherlands East Indies trade talks.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Regarding Tokyo Monthly Political Report for May 1934

subfiles.about: Despatch No. 823 from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew transmitting the monthly report on conditions in Japan for May 1934.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew transmits Report No. 92 covering Japanese political, diplomatic, and economic developments during May 1934. The report analyzes official and press reactions to the American aide-mémoire following the controversial Amau statement, Prince Konoye's trip to the United States, and Japan's demand for naval parity at the upcoming naval conference. It further details economic policy coordination with Manchukuo, foreign commercial activities, and Japanese diplomatic initiatives toward China led by Minister Ariyoshi.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 823 Transmitting Monthly Report on Conditions in Japan During the Month of May, 1934
